findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path causes process abort instead of returning a typed error to the caller
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? operator instead of unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or empty second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with non-numeric value causes process abort instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use map_err on parse() to convert ParseError into a domain error, and propagate via Result

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values >= 65536
findings.failure_mode: sensor value 70000 becomes 4464 without any error, silently corrupting domain data and making illegal states representable
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and return a typed OverflowError, or validate range with checked_into()

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> for a two-field CSV line when split_once suffices
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line and per field clone; performance degrades linearly with line count and field count
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value parts directly; trim and parse each part without collecting into Vec

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec<String> - panics if line has zero fields (empty line)
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with no comma causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use get(0) with match/if-let, or use split_once which returns Option and short-circuits gracefully

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing - panics if line has only one comma-separated field
findings.failure_mode: line like 'sensor_a,' or 'sensor_a' with no second field causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use get(1) or split_once(',') which returns Option for second part, handling missing fields gracefully

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden I/O side effect inside load_sensors data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: pure data loading has observable side effects; breaks referential transparency, makes testing harder, and couples the core to stdout
findings.fix: Remove println entirely, or return a separate diagnostic/trace collection from the shell layer; the core should be side-effect-free

findings.problem: load_sensors mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string on line 9) with parsing logic (map + collect), violating the shell/core split
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation; any test must touch the filesystem or mock fs module
findings.fix: Split into a pure fn parse_records(lines: impl Iterator<Item = &str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell fn load_sensors(path: &str) that calls fs::read_to_string then delegates to parse_records

findings.problem: Record struct uses raw String and u16 with no invariants - empty name and any u16 value are constructable
findings.failure_mode: Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 } is a valid value that likely violates domain rules (empty sensor name)
findings.fix: Add a named constructor Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Record, Error> that validates name is non-empty; or use a Name newtype with its own invariant

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no error type - all failure modes (I/O, parse, overflow, missing fields) are lost
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish file-not-found from malformed CSV from integer overflow; error handling is impossible
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum (e.g., enum SensorError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse(String), Overflow(String), MissingField(usize) }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError>

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocation per line with .to_string() clones for every field - no try_reserve or checked capacity
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocations; if capacity planning were needed there is no try_reserve usage and allocation failures are unhandled
findings.fix: Avoid Vec allocation entirely by using split_once; when Vec is needed for multi-field records, compute size and use try_reserve with allocation-failure handling

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput; the function does heap allocation per line and per field with no measured performance claim
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify whether the allocation-heavy parsing is acceptable for the target workload; regression risk is unbounded
findings.fix: Add a criterion/cargo-bench benchmark measuring records-per-second for representative file sizes (small, medium, large)

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (flame graph or cpuprofiler) for hot path analysis
no allocation tracking (dhat, valgrind, or heaptrace) for per-record allocation cost
no second-ring tests (property-based, fuzz, or edge-case matrix) for malformed CSV input
no command-line integration test or CLI entry point evidence
residual_risk: This is a static review with no commands run. The crate has 7 BLOCKER and 2 MAJOR violations spanning unwrap usage, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O, absent error types, and missing domain invariants. The code must be refactored to return Result types with domain error enums, remove all unwrap/cast/index, eliminate println side effects, split I/O from parsing into functional core/shell, and add benchmarks before it is delivery-ready.
